title: pkix-path cannot parse pre-1970 UTCTime: PKITS 4.2.3 fails, diff-harness red on main since 2026-11-16
description:
## Observed

NIST PKITS "4.2.3 Valid pre2000 UTC notBefore Date Test3" fails to parse:

  malformed ASN.1 DER value for UTCTime at DER byte 114

The certificate is pkix-path/tests/pkits/certs/Validpre2000UTCnotBeforeDateTest3EE.crt. openssl reads it without complaint:

  notBefore=Jan  1 12:01:00 1950 GMT
  notAfter=Dec 31 08:30:00 2030 GMT

   99:d=3 hl=2 l=13 prim: UTCTIME :500101120100Z
  114:d=3 hl=2 l=13 prim: UTCTIME :301231083000Z

Reproduced locally straight through x509_cert::Certificate::from_der, so this is not a path-validation issue. The certificate never parses at all.

## Why this is a real bug, not a bad fixture

RFC 5280 section 4.1.2.5.1 defines UTCTime as spanning 1950-2049: "Where YY is greater than or equal to 50, the year SHALL be interpreted as 19YY; and where YY is less than 50, the year SHALL be interpreted as 20YY."

So notBefore=1950 is legal, and PKITS classes this chain as VALID -- the test exists precisely to check that a pre-2000 UTCTime is accepted. A library that cannot parse it rejects certificates RFC 5280 permits.

## Likely cause, to confirm before fixing

der's UtcTime is backed by a duration since the Unix epoch, which cannot represent a pre-1970 instant. That would explain rejecting 1950.

But note the reported offset: byte 114 is the notAfter field, an ordinary 2030 value that should decode without trouble. Byte 99 is the 1950 notBefore. So either the offset is misattributed, or the failure surfaces only when the Validity SEQUENCE completes. Pin that down first, because it decides whether the fix belongs in der, in a local UTCTime decode, or only in the error reporting.

Decode the two UTCTime values in isolation before touching anything.

## How this surfaced: a CI gate nobody was reading

.github/workflows/diff-harness.yml has been FAILING on main since at least 2026-11-16 -- three consecutive failures on main pushes. I did not know the workflow existed; it turned up in gh run list after today's push.

It compares the PKITS verdict-class summary against pkix-difftest/baseline-pkits.json and reports:

  -    "Agreement": 71,              +    "Agreement": 63,
  -    "DiagnosticDivergence": 49,   +    "DiagnosticDivergence": 58,

Eight chains moved from Agreement to DiagnosticDivergence against the committed baseline. Whether that drift is this parse bug, the oracle issue below, or an unrelated regression is NOT yet established -- do not assume.

Two harness errors per run:

1. pkix-path on "4.2.3 Valid pre2000 UTC notBefore Date Test3" -- this bug.
2. pyca on "4.1.5 Valid DSA Parameter Inheritance Test5" -- pyca's ASN.1 parser rejects an SPKI with inherited/absent DSA parameters. That is an oracle limitation rather than a pkix-path defect, and probably belongs as an expected skip instead of a harness error.

## Why P1

A parse failure on a certificate RFC 5280 allows is a correctness bug in the core crate, and pkix-path is published at 0.4.0 on crates.io, so this affects real consumers.

Separately, and worth stating plainly: a red CI gate on main that nobody reads is worse than no gate. It was the one signal that would have caught the eight-chain drift, and it had been red for over a week while work continued on top of it.

## Acceptance

[ ] Cause confirmed by decoding both UTCTime values in isolation, and the misattributed byte offset explained
[ ] Pre-1970 UTCTime parses; or the limitation is documented with its reason and PKITS 4.2.3 becomes an explicit expected-failure rather than a silent harness error
[ ] The eight-chain Agreement/DiagnosticDivergence drift explained -- fixed, or the baseline updated with the reason recorded
[ ] The pyca DSA-parameter-inheritance case classified as an oracle skip
[ ] diff-harness green on main
